    (package private) void
    testClosedLoopCorrectsInitialAttitudeError()
    Checks that the closed loop corrects an initial attitude error: with error-free kinematics, an INS whose yaw starts 2 degrees off and a noisy fix every second on a trajectory with speed and heading changes, the yaw error decreases, the corrected attitude remains a valid rotation and the position error ends up below three standard deviations of the fix noise.
    (package private) void
    testClosedLoopTracksTruth()
    Checks the closed loop on a trajectory with speed and heading changes, tactical grade IMU errors and a noisy fix every second: after convergence the position error stays below three standard deviations of the fix noise, it ends up smaller than the error of the INS-only solution for the same data, and it is consistent with the estimated covariance.
    (package private) void
    testConstructor()
     
    (package private) void
    testEpochGateAcceptsExactInterval()
    Checks the epoch gate of position and velocity fixes: fixes arriving exactly one epoch interval apart are accepted, while fixes arriving earlier, or repeating a timestamp, are ignored.
    (package private) void
    testEpochGateToleratesRoundingErrors()
    Checks that a fix arriving one epoch interval after the previous epoch is accepted even when the difference of both timestamps is rounded below the epoch interval (0.7 - 0.2 is lower than 0.5 in floating point arithmetic).
    (package private) void
    testEpochGateWithZeroEpochInterval()
    Checks that with a zero epoch interval only fixes that do not advance time are ignored.
    (package private) void
    testEveryImuSampleCountsWithinEpoch()
    Checks that IMU samples arriving within a Kalman epoch interval are all integrated: with a 1 s epoch interval and 100 Hz samples of a body that accelerates and then decelerates, the frame must equal the per-sample integration, not a single step using only the last sample.
    (package private) void
    testFirstEpochPropagatesOverElapsedTime()
    Checks that the first Kalman filter epoch propagates the covariance over the time elapsed since the first IMU sample: an estimator that has integrated IMU samples before its first fix must end with a different covariance (and a larger gyroscope bias uncertainty) than an estimator receiving the same fix with no elapsed time.
    (package private) void
    testFixCorrectsTowardsMeasurement()
    Checks that a position and velocity fix corrects the INS solution towards the measurement: with the INS initialised 10 m north of the truth, a fix at the true position reduces the position error, moves the solution towards the fix and reduces the position covariance.
    (package private) void
    testFreeFall()
    Checks that with zero specific force the body falls freely: after 1 s from rest the displacement must be g * t^2 / 2 and the velocity g * t along the local gravity vector.

    • YAW_TOLERANCE

      private static final double YAW_TOLERANCE
      Tolerance, in radians, for the yaw integrated over the yawing trajectory. The kinematics generated by ECEFKinematicsEstimator are the exact inverse of the attitude update of ECEFInertialNavigator up to rounding errors, which after 1000 samples remain several orders of magnitude below this value; 1e-6 rad (0.2 arc-seconds) is far below the 1 rad that is lost when rotation is not integrated.
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • TRUTH_POSITION_TOLERANCE

      private static final double TRUTH_POSITION_TOLERANCE
      Tolerance, in meters, for the position reached against the analytic truth of a trajectory. The navigator integrates position with the trapezoidal rule (eq. 5.38), whose error for the centripetal acceleration of a 10 m/s motion over the Earth (1.6e-5 m/s^2) sampled at 100 Hz is well below a micrometer; 1e-3 m leaves margin for the truth integration while being five orders of magnitude below the 100 m travelled.
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • CHAIN_POSITION_TOLERANCE

      private static final double CHAIN_POSITION_TOLERANCE
      Tolerance, in meters, when comparing against the chained navigator oracle. Both sides execute the same floating point operations, so differences can only come from rounding of ECEF coordinates of magnitude 6.4e6 m (ulp of 1e-9 m).
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • CHAIN_VELOCITY_TOLERANCE

      private static final double CHAIN_VELOCITY_TOLERANCE
      Tolerance, in meters per second, when comparing velocity against the truth or the chained navigator oracle: the navigator velocity update is the exact inverse of the kinematics estimation, so only rounding errors (below 1e-9 m/s) remain.
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • CHAIN_ROTATION_TOLERANCE

      private static final double CHAIN_ROTATION_TOLERANCE
      Tolerance for each element of the body to ECEF rotation matrix when comparing against the chained navigator oracle: elements are bounded by one and both sides execute the same operations, so differences are bounded by accumulated rounding (1e-13 after 1000 samples).
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • FREE_FALL_POSITION_TOLERANCE

      private static final double FREE_FALL_POSITION_TOLERANCE
      Tolerance, in meters, for the displacement of a 1 s free fall against g * t^2 / 2. The constant gravity approximation neglects the Coriolis acceleration (2 * 7.29e-5 rad/s * 9.8 m/s = 1.4e-3 m/s^2 at most, i.e. 2.4e-4 m after 1 s) and the gravity gradient (3e-6 s^-2 * 4.9 m); 1e-2 m bounds both with margin while being 500 times smaller than the 4.9 m fallen.
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • FREE_FALL_VELOCITY_TOLERANCE

      private static final double FREE_FALL_VELOCITY_TOLERANCE
      Tolerance, in meters per second, for the velocity gained in a 1 s free fall against g * t. The neglected Coriolis term integrates to 7.29e-5 rad/s * 9.8 m/s^2 * (1 s)^2 = 7.1e-4 m/s at most, hence 1e-3 m/s.
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • UPDATE_FREE_FALL_POSITION_TOLERANCE

      private static final double UPDATE_FREE_FALL_POSITION_TOLERANCE
      Tolerance, in meters, for the displacement of a free fall of up to 1 s starting with a speed of up to 3.5 m/s (2 m/s per axis) against v0 * t + g * t^2 / 2. The neglected Coriolis acceleration is at most 2 * 7.29e-5 rad/s * (3.5 + 9.8) m/s = 1.9e-3 m/s^2, i.e. 1e-3 m after 1 s, and the gravity gradient over the 8.4 m travelled adds 3e-6 s^-2 * 8.4 m = 2.5e-5 m/s^2; hence 1e-2 m.
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • UPDATE_FREE_FALL_VELOCITY_TOLERANCE

      private static final double UPDATE_FREE_FALL_VELOCITY_TOLERANCE
      Tolerance, in meters per second, for the velocity of a free fall of up to 1 s starting with a speed of up to 3.5 m/s against v0 + g * t: the neglected Coriolis acceleration (1.9e-3 m/s^2 at most, see UPDATE_FREE_FALL_POSITION_TOLERANCE) integrates to 1.9e-3 m/s; hence 5e-3 m/s.
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • feed

      private static int feed(INSLooselyCoupledKalmanFilteredEstimator estimator, KalmanFilteredEstimatorTrajectory trajectory) throws com.irurueta.navigation.LockedException, com.irurueta.navigation.NotReadyException, INSException
      Feeds a whole trajectory to an estimator: the first kinematics sample is provided at the start time (which only initialises the estimator), then one sample at the end of each sample interval.
      Parameters:
      estimator - estimator to be fed.
      trajectory - trajectory providing the error-free kinematics.
      Returns:
      number of samples accepted by the estimator.
      Throws:
      com.irurueta.navigation.LockedException - if estimator is locked.

    • assertUpdateIntegratesSample

      private com.irurueta.navigation.frames.ECEFFrame assertUpdateIntegratesSample(com.irurueta.navigation.frames.ECEFFrame frame, BodyKinematics kinematics, double timeSeconds) throws com.irurueta.navigation.LockedException, com.irurueta.navigation.NotReadyException, INSException, InertialNavigatorException
      Checks the behaviour of update for the first two samples: the first one only initialises the estimator (state created from the frame, no navigation, no Kalman filter epoch), a repeated or older timestamp is ignored, and the second one is integrated with the ECEF inertial navigation equations over the elapsed interval.
      Parameters:
      frame - initial frame. It is updated in place by the estimator.
      kinematics - kinematics provided on both samples.
      timeSeconds - timestamp of the first sample, and interval up to the second one, expressed in seconds.
      Returns:
      frame estimated after the second sample.
      Throws:
      com.irurueta.navigation.LockedException - if estimator is locked.
      com.irurueta.navigation.NotReadyException - if estimator is not ready.
      INSException - if estimation fails.
      InertialNavigatorException - if the oracle navigation fails.

    • assertFreeFall

      private static void assertFreeFall(com.irurueta.navigation.frames.ECEFFrame initialFrame, com.irurueta.navigation.frames.ECEFFrame result, double duration, double positionTolerance, double velocityTolerance)
      Asserts that a frame is the result of a free fall from an initial frame: displacement v0 * t + g * t^2 / 2 and velocity v0 + g * t, where g is the gravity at the initial position.
      Parameters:
      initialFrame - frame at the start of the fall.
      result - frame at the end of the fall.
      duration - duration of the fall expressed in seconds.
      positionTolerance - tolerance of the displacement expressed in meters.
      velocityTolerance - tolerance of the velocity expressed in meters per second.
